definition.description: Travel forward on a clear level lane through alternating step-hop cycles. Each side performs one supported step followed by a brief flight and landing before the opposite side repeats; recover the thigh toward the declared landmark, return the contact close beneath the body, stay tall, and coordinate opposite arm and leg. One cycle is one step-hop landing on each side. This excludes no-flight A-March, running, B-Skip, stationary skipping, wall support, resistance, obstacle spacing, a terminal sprint, and assessment.

environment.surface: clear, level, dry, non-slip, impact-appropriate lane
environment.space: one protected 10-20 metre lane with a safe finish zone and no cross traffic
inspection: surface traction, debris, moisture, and clearance
footwear, communication, entry, exit, and coach sightline
environment.changeRule: Changing flight, step-hop contact sequence, support, travel, lane, thigh target, arm action, cadence, resistance, cue, dose, surface, footwear, intent, or symptoms requires revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: safe lane and comfortable pain-free low hop
can demonstrate controlled no-flight A-March before adding flight
understands alternating step-hop rhythm, contact count, stop signal, and exit
session foot, calf, landing, impact, and technical-fatigue budgets fit
excludeOrEscalate: pain, limp, repeated rhythm loss, unsafe lane, or communication conflict
sharp, increasing, unfamiliar, neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or coordination concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal thigh height, cadence, lane length, contact cap, dose, recovery, sprint outcome, readiness threshold, or clinical clearance

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 95 and the A-series sprint-drills research packet: A-Skip is an alternating step-hop with flight; punch and snap-down cue emphasis preserve identity while no-flight marching, running, B-Skip, support, resistance, spacing, and terminal transitions do not.

anatomy.laterality: alternating left-right step-hop cycles; record contacts and any asymmetry by side
anatomy.claimsBoundary: Describes task mechanics and plausible loading sites only; it does not diagnose, treat, prevent injury, or guarantee sprint, jump, or approach transfer.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate alternating step-hop coordination practice when the exact contact rhythm, lane, and impact budget fit.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Step-hop and alternate: stay tall, land close beneath you, and use opposite arm and leg.
secondaryCues: keep the flight brief rather than running
use the assigned thigh target without forcing height
do not reach or make contacts loud
stop before rhythm or contact quality changes
expectedSensations: light repeated foot/calf and hip effort
brief alternating flight and landing coordination
unexpectedSensations: pain, limp, sharp foot/calf/tendon sensation, loud contacts, instability, dizziness, or persistent asymmetry
selfChecks: both sides completed the same step-hop rhythm
contact returned close beneath the body

observationChecklist: exact alternating step-hop and brief flight
lane, surface, footwear, clearance, and finish zone
thigh target, contact reach, sound, posture, arm-leg timing, symmetry, and first quality loss
contacts per side, distance, symptoms, rest, and downstream impact demand

faultCorrections.a_march_or_no_flight: rehearse the smaller step-hop rhythm only if the task and readiness fit; otherwise use A-March after revalidation
faultCorrections.running_or_excessive_cadence: slow the pass and restore clear step-hop rhythm before continuing
faultCorrections.overstride_or_loud_contact: shorten the pass or cadence and restore a close quiet landing
faultCorrections.rhythm_or_balance_loss: end the pass, add recovery, or choose another reviewed task after revalidation

doNotUseWhen: the intended task is A-March, A-Run, B-Skip, wall-supported, resisted, stationary, obstacle, compound, terminal-sprint, or assessment work
lane, symptoms, landing control, impact budget, supervision, or communication is inadequate

supportOperations.supportEscalation: Stop and escalate unresolved symptoms, unsafe conditions, repeated rhythm loss, or a mismatch between the requested task and the exact A-Skip step-hop contract.
supportOperations.changeImpactPolicy: Any change to flight, support, travel, cadence, resistance, cue, dose, surface, or substitute reruns selection, fatigue, impact, logistics, duration, substitutions, and validation.

sourceVariant.archiveReason: The source does not declare an exact step-hop/flight cycle, contact count, lane, dose, fatigue, alternate, or review contract.

legacy.description: Traveling alternating A-Skip step-hop rhythm with brief flight.
legacy.tempo: controlled alternating step-hop; full reset before rhythm or contact quality loss
legacy.loadNote: Bodyweight alternating flight and landing contacts; exact contact cap and recovery are delivery-profile specific.
legacy.cardSummary: Candidate A-Skip with explicit step-hop, flight, alternating landing, lane, and arm-leg coordination boundaries.
legacy.coachLanguage: Define the step-hop rhythm and lane, count contacts per side, and end the pass before landing or rhythm quality changes.
legacy.athleteLanguage: Skip forward with a clear step-hop on both sides, land close beneath you, and stop for symptoms or lost rhythm.

safety.prerequisiteNotes: Readiness is the exact low-hop, landing, lane, symptom, communication, impact-budget, and fatigue context—not a participant classification.
readinessChecks: safe clear lane and finish zone
comfortable controlled low hop and landing
can demonstrate the lower-impact A-March pattern
session impact and technical-fatigue budgets fit
stopSigns: pain, limp, loss of balance, unsafe finish, or participant stop request
loud contacts, repeated reaching, rhythm loss, marked asymmetry, or inability to restore a clear step-hop after rest
contraindications: symptom, unsafe lane, inadequate landing control, impact budget, supervision, or communication
no-flight, running, B-Skip, support, resistance, obstacle, compound, terminal-sprint, or assessment intent without a separately reviewed contract
commonSubstitutions: Use another reviewed task only after full revalidation.
Do not automatically substitute A-March, A-Run, B-Skip, wall-supported, resisted, or obstacle A-Skip work.

score.reviewNotes: Candidate task-only reassessment from focused A-series sprint-drills evidence; independent calibration remains required.

difficultyProfile.notes: Exact traveling alternating step-hop A-Skip contract only.

deliveryProfiles.purpose: Candidate low-dose A-Skip rhythm preparation after no-flight pattern ownership.

dosage.countRule: count only alternating step-hop cycles with brief flight, quiet close landing, tall posture, and reciprocal arm action

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: Each side keeps the same clear step-hop rhythm, brief flight, close quiet landing, tall posture, arm-leg timing, and no stop symptom.
stopRules: stop for pain, limp, balance loss, unsafe lane, or participant request
stop when contacts become loud, reaching, asymmetric, running-like, or rhythm cannot recover after rest
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Confirm A-March ownership, define lane and contacts per side, observe the step-hop from side and rear, and end the pass before contact quality declines.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Use the same step-hop on both sides, stay tall, land close beneath you, and take the full walk-back or rest.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate step-hop coordination practice only; no guaranteed sprint or jump outcome is claimed.

doseScaling.reduce: shorten the lane, reduce contacts or cadence, lengthen rest, or use A-March or another reviewed task after revalidation
doseScaling.doNotAutoProgress: Do not add running, resistance, height, travel constraints, obstacles, a terminal sprint, or fatigue density automatically.

supportPrompts.athlete: Clear step-hop, quiet close contact, full reset.
supportPrompts.coach: Flight and contact count are part of the exact dose.
